greek: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
hint: The oldest manuscripts carry no spaces, no accents, no lower case. Word division is already an act of interpretation.

notes.text: ἀρχή holds together two things English must split: the temporal origin-point, and ruling precedence. The second sense is alive in ἄρχων, *ruler*, and in the ἀρχ- of every English word from *monarch* to *architect*. Neither sense is optional here.

Aorist active indicative, 3rd singular, of ποιέω — the everyday verb for making and doing, used of potters, poets, and God alike. [[flag]] Hebrew *bārā'* is a verb that in this stem never takes a human subject. ποιέω takes any subject at all. The exclusivity — *this is a thing only God does* — is not in the Greek.
Articular: *the* God, the known and definite one. Renders Hebrew *Elohim*, plural in form but taking singular agreement. Greek has no way to show that and does not try.
Singular. Hebrew *šāmayim* is a dual or plural form — *heavens*. The LXX collapses it to one vaulted arch.

γῆ runs from soil underfoot, to farmland, to a country, to dry land as against the sea, to the whole terrestrial realm. Pairing it with οὐρανός pulls toward the widest sense without cancelling the narrow ones.

*God* is capitalised because the lexicon prints it so. The pronouns standing for God in the chain are not: *he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out*. The manuscripts have no lower case, so a reverential capital is never in the text — it is an editorial decision, and this rendering does not make it.

reading: [[in beginning|within, inside of, and by means of the first moment, the origin-point, the source, the first principle from which a thing proceeds, and simultaneously the headship, the rule, and the governing precedence over all that follows|ἐν; ἀρχή]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]], [[made|made, did, made / produced / created, composed / wrote, made / represented in poetry, described in verse, put into verse, brought to pass / brought about / caused, held, acted, worked / operated|ποιέω]] [[the heaven|the heaven, the vault / firmament of heaven / sky, the region of heaven / climate|οὐρανός]]; and [[the earth|the earth, the land, the land / country, the earth / ground, the lump of earth|γῆ]].

greek: ἡ δὲ γῆ ἦν ἀόρατος καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος, καὶ σκότος ἐπάνω τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἐπεφέρετο ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος.
hint: Closed, the line is what a fourth-century reader actually met on the page.

notes.text: A soft adversative, not the hard ἀλλά. It pivots the narrative without contradicting what came before: *however, whereas, on the other hand*.
Imperfect of εἰμί. Durative — a condition that held and kept holding, not a snapshot. English *was* is aspectually blank, so the duration has to be spelled out.

The single largest departure in the verse, and possibly in the chapter. Hebrew *tōhû wā-bōhû* is desolation and emptiness — trackless waste, ruin, the wilderness where nothing is. The Greek says *invisible and un-outfitted*: a thing that exists but is neither perceptible nor yet furnished. On this reading Philo and much of the patristic tradition built a pre-cosmic, formless substrate. It is not what the Hebrew says.
Un-seeable, not presenting itself to sight. The same word Paul uses of God himself — *the image of the invisible God*, Col 1:15.
Built on κατασκευή: the full outfitting of a house or a ship — fittings, provisions, installed equipment. *Formless* is too abstract; the word means *not yet fitted out*.
a-βυσσος, *without a sounding* — a depth no plumb line reaches. Renders Hebrew *tĕhôm*, the primeval deep.
Anarthrous. πνεῦμα and Hebrew *rûaḥ* share the same triple range — wind, breath, spirit — one of the rare places where the two languages line up exactly and nothing at all is lost.

Imperfect middle-passive of ἐπιφέρω, *to be borne upon*. Hebrew *mĕraḥepet* is a bird word — hovering, fluttering, brooding over young, used of an eagle over the nest in Deut 32:11. The Greek is a current, not a wing.
The familiar *face of the waters* is not here. The Hebrew has *face of* at both points; the LXX drops it at both. ὕδατος is also singular against Hebrew plural *mayim*.

πνεῦμα is printed lowercase in both reading texts. The manuscripts have no lower case at all, so a capital is never in the text: *Spirit* with a capital would decide for the reader that the word is a title.

reading: [[but|but, however, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[the earth|the earth, the land, the land / country, the earth / ground, the lump of earth|γῆ]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[unseen|unseen / not to be seen / invisible, without sight|ἀόρατος]]; and [[not properly prepared|not properly prepared, unwrought / unformed, chaos, unpolished / unartificial|ἀκατασκεύαστος]]. And [[darkness|darkness / gloom, the darkness of death|σκότος]] was [[above|above / atop / on the upper side / part, above / more than|ἐπάνω]] [[of the great deep|of the great deep / abyss / bottomless pit, of the unfathomable / enormous|ἄβυσσος]]. And [[blowing|blowing, a wind / blast, a breeze / influence, breathed air / breath, the ghost, that which is breathed forth / odour / scent, spirit, inspiration, the Holy Spirit, angels, evil spirits|πνεῦμα]] — [[of God|of everything that God is by nature, of deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]] — [[was being brought|was being brought / put / laid upon, was being attacked / assailed, was being brought with, was being imputed, was being conferred / imposed upon, was being added to / increased, was being brought with / upon oneself / brought as dowry, was being rushed upon or after / attacked / assaulted, was being borne onwards, was being come after / next / ensued|ἐπιφέρω]] [[above|above / atop / on the upper side / part, above / more than|ἐπάνω]] [[of the water|of the water, of the waters, of the rain-water / rain, of the water of the water-clock|ὕδωρ]].
